intro: A model can fail before learning starts when padding, stride, and dilation produce an unexpected spatial shape.
task: Compute the two spatial output dimensions for a convolution with per-axis kernel, stride, symmetric padding, and dilation.
requirements: Each argument is a two-element list or tuple of integers; booleans are invalid.
Input shape, kernel, stride, and dilation are positive. Padding is nonnegative and applied on both sides of its axis.
Use the effective kernel dilation * (kernel - 1) + 1. Reject a kernel that cannot fit after padding; return a Python tuple.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Compute effective kernel size before considering the stride.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Padding contributes twice its value; a partially fitting final window is discarded.

explanation: Dilation spaces kernel taps apart, increasing the effective receptive field without increasing the number of weights. Padding adds available positions on both sides.
After subtracting effective kernel size from the padded input, integer division by stride counts complete shifts. Add one for the starting position.
Compare a three-tap kernel at dilation one and two. Explain why both have three weights while their required input span differs.
